subject: Post-call recap: NovoHealth workload velocity, QPS windowing & streaming needs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novohealth.com>, Leah O'Connor <procurement@novohealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: NovoHealth workload velocity, QPS windowing & streaming needs

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from the call and the follow-ups we promised: 

What we captured (high level)
- Primary use case: clinical note summarization + real-time Q&A in the web app. Most calls are user-initiated summaries and short chat sessions.
- Latency SLOs discussed: target 95th <= 300ms for non-streamed generation at ~512 tokens; streaming to client for longer sessions with p50 chunk latency goal <= 100ms.
- Streaming: roughly a third of user flows may use streaming (we'll confirm exact fraction).

Questions / clarifications we need from you (to size reliably) — please fill or confirm the values below if possible: 
1) Steady-state QPS (average sustained over business hours) and typical peak QPS windows (duration, cadence).
2) Average tokens per response and 95th/99th token lengths (we need both typical and worst-case token counts).
3) What percent of requests use streaming vs full-response? For streaming: typical chunk size (tokens) and target inter-chunk latency.
4) Concurrency per user/session (e.g., how many parallel requests per user) and any known bot/batch patterns.
5) Geographic split (US/EU/APAC) and whether EU traffic needs to be pinned to EU hosts.
6) Any regulatory constraints around retention or on-prem routing for subsets of traffic.

Next steps proposed from Redwood: 
- If you can send a brief workload snapshot (attachment: Novo_workload_form.xlsx) with the items above we’ll run a sizing runbook and propose an initial Dedicated pool and a couple of streaming-config options.
- Suggested PoC: 2-week calibration with synthetic replay of a representative day (we'll need a sample trace or histogram).

I attached a short workload form and a one-pager on streaming patterns we discussed. Rishi and Soojin are on copy to help with sizing once we get the numbers.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: novo_workload_form.xlsx (spreadsheet), streaming-patterns.pdf (one-pager)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novohealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah O'Connor <procurement@novohealth.com>, Engineering Team <eng@novohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: NovoHealth workload velocity, QPS windowing & streaming needs

Hey Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. I filled in the highlights below from our side (high-confidence numbers in bold). I'll attach a short export of our production request histogram by EOD.

1) Steady-state / peak QPS:
   - Steady-state (business hours): ~25 QPS sustained (US region)
   - Typical peak events: spikes up to ~450 QPS, usually lasting 2-5 minutes (happen 1-3x/day tied to shift changes & batch job completions)
2) Tokens per response:
   - Average response tokens: ~320 tokens
   - 95th percentile: ~820 tokens
   - Absolute max observed: ~1,200 tokens (rare)
3) Streaming vs full responses:
   - ~35% of interactive sessions use streaming (mostly chat UI)
   - Streaming chunk: ~20-40 tokens per chunk; target perceived latency <= 100ms per chunk
4) Concurrency per user/session:
   - Typical concurrent requests per active user: 1-2. Heavy power users may hit 4 concurrently.
   - Bot/batch: 2% of traffic is scheduled batches that fan out many concurrent requests for backfill.
5) Geo split:
   - ~85% US, ~10% EU, ~5% APAC. EU traffic needs to be routed to EU due to data localization (we'll provide CIAM tags).
6) Retention/regulatory:
   - Nothing exceeding what we discussed; logs kept for 90 days.

One more ask: for the streaming flows, are there recommended chunking strategies to reduce overall token cost while keeping perceived latency low? Also curious about KV-prefix caching — worth discussing if we can reduce repeated prompt tokens for certain flows.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
NovoHealth
samir.patel@novohealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novohealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Leah O'Connor <procurement@novohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: NovoHealth workload velocity, QPS windowing & streaming needs

Samir — perfect, this is exactly what we need to run a sizing pass. Quick notes from the Redwood sizing playbook given your numbers:

- Baseline tokens/sec (steady-state): 25 QPS * 320 tokens = ~8,000 tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak moment (worst-case): 450 QPS * 820 tokens (95th) = ~369,000 tokens/sec for the short spike window.
- Streaming traffic: with ~35% streaming and 20–40 token chunks, we should account for more frequent small-slice generation and prioritize lower p50 chunk latency.
- Concurrency: assume up to 4 concurrent requests per active user for capacity planning; account for the 2% batch fan-out as a burst factor.

Preliminary recommendation (rough, for discussion):
- Hosted/Dedicated mix: start with a small Dedicated pool sized to cover ~2x steady-state (to provide headroom and reduce cold-starts) and rely on Hosted surge capacity for the daily short peaks, OR if you require deterministic latency during peaks we can size Dedicated to cover the 95th-peak.
- Suggested trial config: Dedicated 4x A100-ish-equivalent backends (we'll provide exact vGPU mapping once we calibrate with your sample trace) + streaming-optimized runtime (smaller generation batches, lower prefetch).
- Caching: KV/prefix caching can cut repeated prompt tokens significantly if you have repeated system/context text — Rishi will follow up on cache viability and how to integrate with your session model.

We attached a very rough CSV with the calculations (proposed-sizing-rough.csv). If you can share the request histogram and a sample of 1k requests (anonymized), Rishi & Soojin can run a simulation and send back a recommended Dedicated size and a throughput-to-cost estimate.

Next actions:
- Samir: send histogram + sample (anonymized) by Thu 22 Jul if possible.
- Rishi: run sizing simulation and share results + a couple of config options by Fri 23 Jul.
- Leah: let us know rough procurement timeline so we can align PoC window with approvals.

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if that helps — we can also run the simulation live with your trace.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-sizing-rough.csv (estimates)
